title: Sarah Steffens named 2027 Missouri Teacher of the Year by DESE
text:
Sarah Steffens named 2027 Missouri Teacher of the Year by DESE
By E. M. Blum
Sarah Steffens, a K–4 Reading Interventionist at Elm Grove Elementary in the Fort Osage R‑I School District, was named the 2027 Missouri Teacher of the Year by the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education on Sep. 16.
Steffens was recognized for her commitment to student literacy, innovative instructional leadership, and her impact on early learners within her school community. Dr. Stacey Preis, Interim Commissioner of Education, said, “Sarah Steffens exemplifies the dedication and skill we see in outstanding Missouri educators. Steffens is celebrated for empowering student voice, strengthening literacy growth, and building strong, collaborative relationships with colleagues and families. Her work reflects the best of our schools and the deep impact teachers have on students across the state.”
Steffens was originally announced as one of seven statewide finalists for this honor. The selection process began with 35 Regional Teachers of the Year before narrowing to 16 statewide semifinalists from districts across Missouri. A committee composed of former Missouri Teachers of the Year and representatives from education organizations interviewed finalists in early September before naming Steffens as this year’s honoree.
As Missouri’s Teacher of the Year for 2027, Steffens will represent Missouri in the National Teacher of the Year competition and serve as an ambassador for educational excellence throughout her term.
The Teacher of the Year program recognizes outstanding teachers who demonstrate exceptional instructional practices and leadership within their schools and communities while promoting student achievement. Honorees participate in mentoring activities, speaking engagements, and initiatives that support teaching across Missouri.
The Department of Elementary and Secondary Education supports school accountability through programs such as the Missouri School Improvement Program; serves all 557 public school districts and charter schools; manages public education from kindergarten through twelfth grade as well as early childhood initiatives; is led by a Commissioner of Education; operates statewide; and coordinates federal programs such as Title I funding, according to its official website.
